title: Fix D87 intervention class; derive host-error records from interventions
summary: Change D87's intervention signal in backtest.rs from class 'docs' to 'code' (per decision-sets.md section 9). Add a strict-pattern derivation ('HTTP <code>' plus a merge operation) that turns past interventions into host-error records marked derived and citing the source intervention. The backtest uses those records, so rerunning it should flag D87 via ar1x and nothing else; the real result is reported either way.

defaults_applied.how: Unit and integration tests for the derivation and the backtest; clippy clean.
The report cites the source intervention and states the real backtest result.
The derived marker is a typed field on the record, not a special case in the backtest.
Doc comments explain the derived marker and the exact pattern.
The backtest is run and its result reported.
One change covering both follow-ups; no extra features.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Derived records are held in memory during the backtest and not written under records/ (records/ never changes in a job).
HostError gains an optional provenance field (derived, with the source intervention id). It is absent for observed records, so existing records still parse.

The pattern is matched against the intervention's what and why text: 'HTTP <3-digit code>' plus the word 'merge'. The job, at, and phase come from the intervention (landing phase for a merge). If the intervention has no job, nothing is derived.
Derived records are distinguishable everywhere they are listed, and the report never says the client observed them.
The exact-match intervention signal for D87 also needs the intervention text read in the backtest, so InterventionRow gains what/why or the derivation reads the full record.
Whether the real run flags only D87 depends on records/ data, which I cannot see; the producer reports the actual result.

acceptance_criteria.text: backtest.rs D87's intervention signal uses class_of_work "code" (name and doc comments updated to say code), matching decision-sets.md section 9.
The HostError record carries a derived marker and the source intervention id. An observed record has neither, and record validation rejects a derived record without a source.

A derivation function takes an intervention and returns a derived HostError only when its text matches 'HTTP <code>' plus a merge operation exactly; otherwise it returns none. Unit tests cover a match, a non-match, a missing job, and an out-of-range code.
The backtest report lists derived records separately from observed ones, labels them derived, and cites the source intervention id. D87's firing cites the derived record and, through it, ar1x.

Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`, then `cargo fmt --check`: all pass. This includes a backtest test with a fixture intervention whose text states an HTTP 405 on a merge, showing D87 flagged under review through a derived record, and a fixture with no such text showing nothing flagged.
`cargo run -p athena-cli -- backtest` (or the actual subcommand form) runs. The producer's report states the real result for D87 and for all other decisions, whatever it is.

out_of_scope: Using Jev or any model to derive records.
Changing the landing watcher's behavior on live host errors.
Changing D88 or any decision other than D87.
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: the change spans a record schema, a derivation, and the backtest report, plus tests. The real-data outcome (only D87 flagged) cannot be checked from here.
